headline: Highest risk is medium: social-auto-upload can transmit content to external platforms, but marker is local-only and no shared channel or write conflict is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented: marker has no filesystem read/write, MCP, browser, or network egress, while social-auto-upload is a CLI uploader with no documented ingestion of marker outputs. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added between the agents, injection becomes plausible.
IF social-auto-upload begins parsing marker-generated text as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy marker output into social-auto-upload prompts.
Disable any future shared clipboard or MCP bridge.
Review any wrapper script that forwards text between them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: marker is local-only and touches no data classes, while social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads media via external APIs. There is no documented shared workspace or direct data flow from marker to B, so leakage is limited to unusual operator bridging rather than default behavior.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive documents into social-auto-upload inputs, those contents may leave the local environment.
IF a shared workspace is introduced and marker writes files into it, B could upload them.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the uploader workspace.
Use separate directories for document processing and uploads.
Audit upload inputs before each run.
Restrict social-auto-upload to non-sensitive media.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both profiles explicitly lack filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification capabilities, so there is no overlapping mutable resource to contend over. social-auto-upload supports multiple instances, but marker cannot write shared state, making a write conflict pathway absent.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF git or shared account files are introduced outside the current profiles, reassess.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Avoid placing them on the same mutable workspace.
Use per-account files for social-auto-upload.
Recheck permissions after any deployment change.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading error path is weak: marker produces document-processing output, but social-auto-upload is a media uploader and there is no documented default pipeline where B treats A's output as authoritative. Any harmful chain requires an operator to manually feed A's output into B.
conditions: IF marker output is copied into social-auto-upload as captions or metadata without review, errors can propagate.
IF B is configured to auto-post generated text from A, the risk rises.
mitigations: Manually review any text before upload.
Separate drafting from posting steps.
Disable auto-posting of generated captions.
Use a checklist for final publication.

E_compliance.rationale: marker has no declared data classes, while social-auto-upload touches account data and media and can send them to third-party platforms. The pair does not show a residency or certification mismatch, but the uploader's external API use creates a modest compliance exposure if regulated content is introduced.
conditions: IF regulated media or personal data is uploaded through social-auto-upload, platform policy and residency obligations may apply.
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the operator's storage and the target platform, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Avoid uploading regulated data.
Confirm platform retention settings before posting.
Document the data class for each upload.
Use a separate account for non-sensitive content.
